newsitem.title: INDIA: Times Guaranty sees Bombay share-index near bottom.
newsitem.headline: Times Guaranty sees Bombay share-index near bottom.

text.p: Investors must be alert for a minor bottom at 2770-2730 points as the decline of the benchmark Bombay stocks index shows signs of weakening, a technical analyst at finance firm Times Guaranty said on Wednesday.
On Tuesday, Bombay's 30-share index fell 53.43 points or 1.87 percent to 2798 -- a three-year low.
"The market has lost 95.09 points over the weekend close of 2890.50. The index is at its three-year low, has made tops and bottoms," technical analyst Mehmood Khan said in a note.
But he said the downtrend was showing signs of weakening.
"The speed of the decline is taking place at the rate of only 40.04 points per trading day as against the speed of 64.10 points for the previous decline from 3176.69 to 2856.21," Khan said.

"Second, the internal extension is equal to 80 percent of the previous decline. For the downtrend to become healthy, the speed must equal or exceed that of the previous decline and the internal extension must exceed 100 percent."
He said investors could take short-term positions with a stop-loss of 2665 points.
